From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline view

The covering note calls this a "fair and balanced package". It is not. The Seller Update describes several items as "addressed", "adequate", "ordinary course" or "settled", but the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts those descriptions:

| Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|
| Bluefen consent "addressed" | No final written consent; conditions not evidenced (DL 2) |
| Riverlark handled by a release after Completion | Not repaid; no discharge of security (DL 3) |
| Ironquay indemnity "adequate" | AUD 180k open; no payment receipt; no assignment (DL 4) |
| Bonuses "a matter for the Seller" | AUD 420k not in the funds flow; on-costs not addressed (DL 5) |
| Incident "not expected to be material" | Access, scope and notification all undetermined (DL 6) |
| Sandbar renewals "ordinary course" | Disclosure expressly declines to say they are ordinary course (DL 8) |

The structural proposals would also cap, time-bar, disclose away and knowledge-bar almost everything. These include general disclosure, the buyer-knowledge bar, limitations applying to all Claims, and title under the general cap. Taken together, the Buyer would be left with very little real recourse on a AUD 24m acquisition.

The identifiable known exposures are roughly:

- Riverlark: AUD 3.2m
- Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs
- Ironquay: AUD 180k
- Sandbar: AUD 330k

That totals about AUD 4.1m+, close to the entire AUD 4.8m general cap, and it excludes Bluefen (30% of revenue) and the privacy incident. These items must be dealt with through price mechanics, conditions and specific indemnities, not the warranty regime.

---

## Part A: Structural / risk-allocation issues

### 1. Fundamental warranties (title and capacity) under the general cap and time limit. **Reject.**
- **Why it matters:** Title is the thing we are buying. A 20% cap and 18-month limit on title would mean a defect in title to 100% of the shares is recoverable only up to AUD 4.8m. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- **Push back:**
  - Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency, no encumbrances over shares, issued share capital) should be capped at 100% of the price.
  - They should have a long time limit, for example 6–7 years. NSW limitation periods are 6 years for simple contract and 12 years for deeds, so consider executing the SPA as a deed.
  - No de minimis, basket or disclosure should apply against them.
- **Title evidence (DD-012):** The share register alone is not enough. The Disclosure Letter (DL 10) itself says it is only the Seller's source. Require:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - original share certificates, or a lost-certificate indemnity;
  - the constitution, with confirmation there are no pre-emptive rights or that they are waived;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and Company showing no security over the shares (relevant given Riverlark);
  - a warranty that there are no options, convertibles, ESOP or other rights to issue shares.

### 2. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/13/20.5). **Reject the default.**
- **Why it matters:** This would place specific indemnities, the tax indemnity, leakage/price-adjustment claims and covenant breaches under the general cap, thresholds and 18-month limit. The specific indemnities would be largely worthless.
- **Push back:**
  - Reverse the default: limitations apply only to Warranty Claims, unless expressly extended.
  - Carve out of all limitations: fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives (including Company management). Note that fraud generally cannot be excluded at law anyway.
  - Specific indemnities, tax, fundamental warranties, covenant/leakage claims and debt-free/cash-free adjustments should sit outside the general cap and thresholds.
  - Non-reliance should be limited to statements outside the SPA and Disclosure Letter. It must not purport to exclude claims for misleading or deceptive conduct where the Seller's conduct is the cause.

### 3. Cap and thresholds (cl 12.1/12.2): negotiable, but improve
- **General cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m):** Not unusual on its own. It is only acceptable if fundamentals, tax and specific indemnities are carved out. If no W&I policy is taken, seek 30–50%. If W&I is taken, the Seller cap could drop materially, but the known issues below will be excluded from W&I cover. Those issues therefore need Seller-backed indemnities plus escrow regardless.
- **De minimis AUD 25k (~0.1%):** Push to around AUD 10–15k. Related claims arising from the same or similar facts should be aggregated for the de minimis test.
- **Basket AUD 250k (~1.04%), deductible ("only the excess"):** Push to a tipping basket (first dollar once exceeded) and/or lower to around 0.5% (AUD 120k). Claims below the de minimis should count toward the basket.
- **18-month general limit:** Acceptable if it covers at least one full audit cycle post-Completion. Tax needs its own regime (see item 11).

### 4. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2). **Reject.**
- **Why it matters:** Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room and all public records shifts the entire diligence risk to the Buyer. Combined with clause 8.3, it removes most warranty protection.
- **Push back:**
  - Only matters "Fairly Disclosed" in the Disclosure Letter should qualify warranties. "Fairly Disclosed" means disclosed with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect of the matter.
  - Delete the general data-room and public-register disclosure. A fallback is to limit it to specifically identified documents, still subject to the fair-disclosure standard.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax, or matters covered by specific indemnities. Disclosure must never cut down an indemnity.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission):** Tolerable, but add that it does not limit or qualify any indemnity or the Seller's obligations.
- **Staleness:** The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, roughly six weeks before today. Require:
  - an updated disclosure only in respect of matters arising after signing;
  - that any update does not cure breaches or limit Buyer remedies;
  - a Buyer termination right for material updates before Completion;
  - a bring-down of warranties at Completion.

### 5. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3). **Reject.**
- **Why it matters:** It covers knowledge of the Buyer and its "advisers", plus anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That imputes constructive knowledge so broadly that diligence itself defeats claims.
- **Push back:** Replace with a pro-sandbagging clause. The Buyer's knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) does not affect any Claim, except to the extent a matter is Fairly Disclosed. A fallback of last resort is limiting the bar to the actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals. It must never apply to indemnities, tax or fundamentals.

---

## Part B: Specific deal issues

### 6. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3/6.3). **Critical. Make it a hard Condition.**
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%). Change-control consent is required under cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. No consent has been obtained and there is no evidence the conditions are satisfied (DL 2).
- **Seller's problems:**
  - "Addressed" is untrue.
  - "Reasonable endeavours" is weak.
  - Treating the consent as satisfied "on delivery of written consent" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions. A consent whose conditions remain unmet may not actually protect the contract.
- **Push back:**
  - Condition Precedent: unconditional written Bluefen consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably).
  - All cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, evidenced and not revoked at Completion.
  - The Seller to use all reasonable/best endeavours.
  - Buyer may participate in Bluefen discussions.
  - Buyer has the sole right to waive the Condition.
  - Sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Fallback if the Buyer waives: an escrow or price adjustment linked to Bluefen termination or adverse renegotiation within X months, and/or a specific indemnity.
  - Confirm whether the DD-006 incident touches Bluefen data. If it does, that could independently give Bluefen termination rights.

### 7. Riverlark facility, about AUD 3.2m (cl 2/7). **Critical. Reject the post-Completion release.**
- **Facts:** Not repaid. A change-control clause (8.1) is likely triggered by Completion. No discharge (DL 3).
- **Why it matters:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A release "following Completion" means the Company is in default or facing acceleration from day one, with security still registered, and the Buyer holding only a promise from the Seller.
- **Push back:**
  - Riverlark must be repaid from the purchase price at Completion through the funds flow, as a deduction for Indebtedness.
  - Completion deliverables: a payout letter (stating principal, interest, break costs and fees to the Completion date), a deed of release of all security and guarantees, and PPSR financing change statements and/or an undertaking to register discharges within a set short period, plus releases of any mortgages.
  - "Approximately" is not acceptable. Use the exact payout figure.
  - Seller warranty and indemnity that no other financial indebtedness exists.

### 8. DD-005 Completion bonuses, AUD 420k. **Must be deducted from the price.**
- **Why it matters:** Saying the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company, and therefore the Buyer, pays them after Completion. The on-costs are unaddressed (DL 5): PAYG withholding, superannuation guarantee (currently 12%), NSW payroll tax and workers' compensation. Total cost is likely around AUD 500k+.
- **Push back:**
  - Define Transaction Bonuses, including all employer on-costs, as Indebtedness or Transaction Costs deducted from the price.
  - Pay them through Company payroll at or shortly after Completion from a funded amount.
  - Where continued-employment conditions defer payment, the full amount is still deducted, held by the Company or in escrow.
  - Seller indemnity for any other change-of-control or retention payments.

### 9. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1). **Indemnity is inadequate.**
- **Facts:** Ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl 7.3). AUD 180k appears open. There is no payment evidence and no assignment (DL 4).
- **Why it matters:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k payment. It is that the Company may not own IP that may be embedded in its product, which exposes it to infringement, injunction or ransom pricing. An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover that.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion: the Seller procures payment of every SOW3 fee, with cleared-funds evidence.
  - A confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay to the Company covering all SOW3 Project Materials, with moral rights consents. Make this a Condition or Completion deliverable.
  - If not obtained: an escrow retention plus a broad specific indemnity covering all loss from any third-party ownership of, or infringement claim relating to, SOW3 materials, including remediation and redevelopment cost. It should be outside the cap and thresholds, with a long time limit and no disclosure against it.
  - Any unpaid SOW3 fees are treated as Indebtedness.

### 10. DD-006 export/privacy incident. **Material; needs a specific indemnity.**
- **Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records were involved (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access and scope are unknown, the notification decision is unresolved, and the investigation is still "preliminary" as at 22 September (DL 6).
- **Why it matters:**
  - Under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment within 30 days. If the incident predates 22 September, that window has likely passed. A still-"preliminary" investigation is itself a compliance risk.
  - Recent Privacy Act amendments increased the OAIC's enforcement tools and penalty exposure.
  - There is also contractual exposure to customers whose data was involved, possibly including Bluefen.
  - "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion. It is unsupported and contradicted by its own Disclosure Letter.
- **Push back:**
  - Before signing or Completion: the full incident file, the forensic or investigation report, the assessment and its date, the notification decision and reasoning (including any OAIC or individual notifications), and confirmation of whether the recipient accessed the file and whether deletion was confirmed.
  - Seller covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications promptly, in consultation with the Buyer.
  - Specific indemnity for all loss from the incident (regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation, notification, customer claims, remediation). It should sit outside the general cap and thresholds, with no disclosure or knowledge defence, a time limit of at least 3–4 years, and Buyer conduct of regulatory matters.
  - Warranties on privacy and security compliance, plus "no other incidents".

### 11. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime." **Reject.**
- **Tax:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including the bonus on-costs and payroll tax.
  - Cap at 100% of the price.
  - Time limit tied to the ATO amendment period plus a buffer, for example the later of 5 years or 60 days after the amendment period expires.
  - No thresholds; no data-room disclosure against it.
  - Covers stamp duty and payroll tax grouping exposure.
- **IP:** As an analytics business, IP is core value. Seek a higher cap or a longer limit (for example, 3 years) for the IP and data warranties. At minimum, exclude IP from the deductible basket.

### 12. Sandbar supplier renewals, 3 × AUD 110k (AUD 330k).
- **Concern:** These are described as "related" and are to be "read together for timing/scope". Three identical AUD 110k renewals may have been split to stay below a conduct-of-business consent threshold or an internal approval limit. The disclosure expressly declines to say they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued (DL 8). Also confirm whether "related" means related to the Seller (a related-party arrangement).
- **Push back:**
  - Obtain all three contracts and the dates entered.
  - Confirm they are arm's length with no Seller affiliation.
  - Confirm the term, termination rights and prepayment or accrual status.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants should aggregate related or connected contracts.
  - If entered during the pre-signing or interim period without consent, or not arm's length: the Seller procures termination at its cost, or the amount is treated as leakage or Indebtedness. Unpaid committed amounts relating to the pre-Completion period go into the working capital or debt adjustment.

### 13. Lower-risk items: confirm and paper
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation only. Add a Seller covenant to give notice on time, and a warranty that no landlord consent or change-of-control right applies.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction only. Confirm no deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording. Obtain a Seller warranty, or comfort from Mossvale if the contract is material.

### 14. Seller covenant strength and security
Harbourglass "Ventures" may distribute proceeds after Completion. Seek:
- an escrow or retention, for example AUD 1.5–2.5m, sized to the Ironquay, privacy and Bluefen exposures, released in stages;
- and/or a parent or fund guarantee;
- plus a restriction on distribution until the general claims period expires.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Title/capacity | General cap, 18 months | 100% price cap, 6–7 years, no thresholds or disclosure; full title deliverables (ASIC, certificates, PPSR) | **Critical** |
| 2 | Scope of limitations | All Claims | Warranty Claims only; carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, fundamentals, leakage | **Critical** |
| 3 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Repay at Completion from price; payout letter, deed of release, PPSR discharges | **Critical** |
| 4 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours | Hard CP covering consent *and* cl 11.3 conditions; best endeavours; sunset; fallback escrow or indemnity | **Critical** |
| 5 | General disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; no disclosure against fundamentals, tax, indemnities; bring-down | **Critical** |
| 6 | Buyer knowledge bar | Broad, incl. advisers and "discoverable" | Pro-sandbagging clause | **Critical** |
| 7 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Off funds flow | Deduct as Indebtedness, plus all on-costs (super, payroll tax, PAYG, workers comp) | High |
| 8 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 fee | Payment plus confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broad uncapped IP indemnity and escrow | High |
| 9 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not material" | Full incident file; NDB compliance confirmation; specific uncapped indemnity; conduct rights | High |
| 10 | Tax / IP warranties | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity (100% cap, ATO-period limit); enhanced IP limits | High |
| 11 | Sandbar AUD 330k | "Ordinary course" | Contracts, related-party check, aggregation in covenants; leakage or Indebtedness treatment if improper | Medium |
| 12 | Cap and thresholds | 20%; AUD 25k; AUD 250k deductible | 30–50% if no W&I; AUD 10–15k de minimis with aggregation; tipping basket ~0.5% | Medium |
| 13 | Credit support | None | Escrow or retention and/or guarantee | High |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only | Covenant to notify; confirmatory warranties | Low |

**Recommended next steps**
1. Send an information request now covering the Bluefen correspondence, the Riverlark payout figure, the Ironquay payment and assignment status, the full DD-006 incident file, the Sandbar contracts and dates, and the bonus on-cost calculation.
2. Decide on W&I insurance, because it drives the cap negotiation. Known issues will be excluded from cover either way.
3. Prepare the mark-up on the basis above, reframing the funds flow so that Riverlark, the bonuses plus on-costs, and any Ironquay arrears are deducted at Completion.

*Caveat: this review is based only on the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter. Clause references and conclusions should be checked against the full SPA draft and the underlying DD documents before the mark-up goes out.*

  - a bring-down of warranties at Completion.

### 5. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3). **Reject.**
- **Why it matters:** It covers knowledge of the Buyer and its "advisers", plus anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. That imputes constructive knowledge so broadly that diligence itself defeats claims.
- **Push back:** Replace with a pro-sandbagging clause. The Buyer's knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed) does not affect any Claim, except to the extent a matter is Fairly Disclosed. A fallback of last resort is limiting the bar to the actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals. It must never apply to indemnities, tax or fundamentals.

## Part B: Specific deal issues

### 6. Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3/6.3). **Critical. Make it a hard Condition.**
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%). Change-control consent is required under cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. No consent has been obtained and there is no evidence the conditions are satisfied (DL 2).
- **Seller's problems:**
  - "Addressed" is untrue.
  - "Reasonable endeavours" is weak.
  - Treating the consent as satisfied "on delivery of written consent" ignores the cl 11.3 conditions. A consent whose conditions remain unmet may not actually protect the contract.
- **Push back:**
  - Condition Precedent: unconditional written Bluefen consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably).
  - All cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, evidenced and not revoked at Completion.
  - The Seller to use all reasonable/best endeavours.
  - Buyer may participate in Bluefen discussions.
  - Buyer has the sole right to waive the Condition.
  - Sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Fallback if the Buyer waives: an escrow or price adjustment linked to Bluefen termination or adverse renegotiation within X months, and/or a specific indemnity.
  - Confirm whether the DD-006 incident touches Bluefen data. If it does, that could independently give Bluefen termination rights.

### 7. Riverlark facility, about AUD 3.2m (cl 2/7). **Critical. Reject the post-Completion release.**
- **Facts:** Not repaid. A change-control clause (8.1) is likely triggered by Completion. No discharge (DL 3).
- **Why it matters:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A release "following Completion" means the Company is in default or facing acceleration from day one, with security still registered, and the Buyer holding only a promise from the Seller.
- **Push back:**
  - Riverlark must be repaid from the purchase price at Completion through the funds flow, as a deduction for Indebtedness.
  - Completion deliverables: a payout letter (stating principal, interest, break costs and fees to the Completion date), a deed of release of all security and guarantees, and PPSR financing change statements and/or an undertaking to register discharges within a set short period, plus releases of any mortgages.
  - "Approximately" is not acceptable. Use the exact payout figure.
  - Seller warranty and indemnity that no other financial indebtedness exists.

### 8. DD-005 Completion bonuses, AUD 420k. **Must be deducted from the price.**
- **Why it matters:** Saying the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company, and therefore the Buyer, pays them after Completion. The on-costs are unaddressed (DL 5): PAYG withholding, superannuation guarantee (currently 12%), NSW payroll tax and workers' compensation. Total cost is likely around AUD 500k+.
- **Push back:**
  - Define Transaction Bonuses, including all employer on-costs, as Indebtedness or Transaction Costs deducted from the price.
  - Pay them through Company payroll at or shortly after Completion from a funded amount.
  - Where continued-employment conditions defer payment, the full amount is still deducted, held by the Company or in escrow.
  - Seller indemnity for any other change-of-control or retention payments.

### 9. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1). **Indemnity is inadequate.**
- **Facts:** Ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl 7.3). AUD 180k appears open. There is no payment evidence and no assignment (DL 4).
- **Why it matters:** The real risk is not the AUD 180k payment. It is that the Company may not own IP that may be embedded in its product, which exposes it to infringement, injunction or ransom pricing. An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover that.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion: the Seller procures payment of every SOW3 fee, with cleared-funds evidence.
  - A confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay to the Company covering all SOW3 Project Materials, with moral rights consents. Make this a Condition or Completion deliverable.
  - If not obtained: an escrow retention plus a broad specific indemnity covering all loss from any third-party ownership of, or infringement claim relating to, SOW3 materials, including remediation and redevelopment cost. It should be outside the cap and thresholds, with a long time limit and no disclosure against it.
  - Any unpaid SOW3 fees are treated as Indebtedness.

### 10. DD-006 export/privacy incident. **Material; needs a specific indemnity.**
- **Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records were involved (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access and scope are unknown, the notification decision is unresolved, and the investigation is still "preliminary" as at 22 September (DL 6).
- **Why it matters:**
  - Under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment within 30 days. If the incident predates 22 September, that window has likely passed. A still-"preliminary" investigation is itself a compliance risk.
  - Recent Privacy Act amendments increased the OAIC's enforcement tools and penalty exposure.
  - There is also contractual exposure to customers whose data was involved, possibly including Bluefen.
  - "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion. It is unsupported and contradicted by its own Disclosure Letter.
- **Push back:**
  - Before signing or Completion: the full incident file, the forensic or investigation report, the assessment and its date, the notification decision and reasoning (including any OAIC or individual notifications), and confirmation of whether the recipient accessed the file and whether deletion was confirmed.
  - Seller covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications promptly, in consultation with the Buyer.
  - Specific indemnity for all loss from the incident (regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation, notification, customer claims, remediation). It should sit outside the general cap and thresholds, with no disclosure or knowledge defence, a time limit of at least 3–4 years, and Buyer conduct of regulatory matters.
  - Warranties on privacy and security compliance, plus "no other incidents".

### 11. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime." **Reject.**
- **Tax:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes, including the bonus on-costs and payroll tax.
  - Cap at 100% of the price.
  - Time limit tied to the ATO amendment period plus a buffer, for example the later of 5 years or 60 days after the amendment period expires.
  - No thresholds; no data-room disclosure against it.
  - Covers stamp duty and payroll tax grouping exposure.
- **IP:** As an analytics business, IP is core value. Seek a higher cap or a longer limit (for example, 3 years) for the IP and data warranties. At minimum, exclude IP from the deductible basket.

### 12. Sandbar supplier renewals, 3 × AUD 110k (AUD 330k).
- **Concern:** These are described as "related" and are to be "read together for timing/scope". Three identical AUD 110k renewals may have been split to stay below a conduct-of-business consent threshold or an internal approval limit. The disclosure expressly declines to say they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued (DL 8). Also confirm whether "related" means related to the Seller (a related-party arrangement).
- **Push back:**
  - Obtain all three contracts and the dates entered.
  - Confirm they are arm's length with no Seller affiliation.
  - Confirm the term, termination rights and prepayment or accrual status.
  - Conduct-of-business covenants should aggregate related or connected contracts.
  - If entered during the pre-signing or interim period without consent, or not arm's length: the Seller procures termination at its cost, or the amount is treated as leakage or Indebtedness. Unpaid committed amounts relating to the pre-Completion period go into the working capital or debt adjustment.

### 13. Lower-risk items: confirm and paper
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation only. Add a Seller covenant to give notice on time, and a warranty that no landlord consent or change-of-control right applies.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction only. Confirm no deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording. Obtain a Seller warranty, or comfort from Mossvale if the contract is material.

### 14. Seller covenant strength and security
Harbourglass "Ventures" may distribute proceeds after Completion. Seek:
- an escrow or retention, for example AUD 1.5–2.5m, sized to the Ironquay, privacy and Bluefen exposures, released in stages;
- and/or a parent or fund guarantee;
- plus a restriction on distribution until the general claims period expires.
